asked.text: The stale rule can break the lock's own guarantee. A lock is stale when it is 'older than mergeLockStaleMin (default 30)' whatever the owner's pid, so a live holder is evicted. A holder can legitimately keep the lock longer than 30 minutes: the CI wait, the main check (up to 15 minutes), and a revert path that waits for the revert PR's CI, merges it, then waits for main again. The takeover is also racy (two waiters can both see a stale lock) and the owner.json write after mkdir leaves a window with a lock and no owner. Recommend: a live pid on this host is never stale; age counts only for another host or a missing or unparseable owner.json; owner.json is renamed into place; takeover is an atomic rename of the directory followed by mkdir.

spikes.answer:
Settled in part; the docs do not give a complete answer.

Writes: by default sandboxed commands can write to the current working directory and its subdirectories, the per-user temp directory, and any --add-dir / permissions.additionalDirectories paths. A sibling directory of the repo is NOT writable by default; it needs an explicit sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite entry (absolute, or ~-relative; on Linux/WSL2 the path must already exist). When the working directory is a linked git worktree, the sandbox already allows writes to the main repository's shared .git directory (so git can update refs and the index), except hooks/ and config inside it, which stay denied. So a lock directory under the git common dir is covered for worktrees without an allowWrite entry, as far as the docs state; the docs do not explicitly name lock directories. Note that the docs' worktree rule is stated for the main repo's shared .git, and the doc does not say whether the sibling worktree path itself needs allowWrite (it is outside cwd, so it likely does).

Network: sandbox.network.allowedDomains starts empty. The docs give no statement that api.github.com or gh needs a specific entry, and do not list it. The docs suggest the alternative for git network commands: excludedCommands such as "git push *" run outside the sandbox with no network proxy restriction. For gh, the docs suggest adding "gh *" to excludedCommands if TLS verification fails on macOS (Go-based CLIs). The docs do not say what allowedDomains must contain for gh to reach api.github.com.

node scripts under .claude/scripts: node is not mentioned anywhere in the sandboxing page. Scripts under .claude/ live inside the working directory, which is readable and writable by default, so the docs imply no allowWrite entry is needed for a script under the cwd; the docs do not address node specifically or .claude/ specifically (note: the protected-path list covers only shell startup files, .gitconfig, .vscode, .idea and .git hooks/config).

Summary: allowWrite needed for the sibling worktree path (per docs, inferred). Shared .git lock dir: covered for linked worktrees per docs. allowedDomains: not settled from the docs (empty by default; no GitHub entry documented). excludedCommands is the documented escape hatch for gh and git network commands.
